title: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)

sections.label: Singapore building up armed forces
sections.summary: Singapore builds up its armed forces to defend against potentially larger aggressors, starting National Service and investing in better technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Thus, Singapore has always had to build up its armed forces in anticipation of having to defend itself against potentially larger aggressors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We tried to overcome the glaring disadvantage of size by starting National Service and investing in better technology.

sections.label: ISIS in Southeast Asia
sections.summary: Southeast Asia is a key ISIS recruitment area, where ISIS established Katibah Nusantara, responsible for the 2016 Jakarta attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The spread of terror continues to be ever present in the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We understand that Southeast Asia is a key recruitment area for the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS) which has established Katibah Nusantara in the region – their fighting force which was responsible for the 2016 Jakarta attacks.

sections.label: Orkim Harmony tanker hijacking
sections.summary: Eight men armed with pistols and machetes hijacked the Orkim Harmony oil tanker and tried to sail it to a friendly harbour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In June last year, eight men armed with pistols and machetes hijacked the Orkim Harmony, an oil tanker carrying some 6,000 tonnes of petrol worth more than $5 million, and tried to sail the ship to a friendly harbour where they could siphon off the liquid cargo.

sections.label: Hybrid warfare threat emerging
sections.summary: Hybrid warfare is emerging, as in Crimea, integrating conventional and unconventional tools by state and non-state actors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The threat of hybrid warfare is also emerging, as we have learnt from the experience of Crimea, where there was a concerted effort to undermine the nation's defences through economic, socio-psychological as well as cyber warfare before taking them on militarily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hybrid warfare integrates conventional and unconventional tools of warfare by both state and non-state actors.

sections.label: Global terrorism index report
sections.summary: The Institute for Economics and Peace assessed terrorism is at an all-time high, with nine times more people killed than in 2000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In fact, in its annual global terrorism index report released at the end of last year, the Institute for Economics and Peace assessed that terrorism is at an all-time high, with more attacks in a wider range of countries than ever before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This index shows that there are nine times more people killed today in terror attacks than in the year 2000.

sections.label: ISIS targeting Southeast Asia
sections.summary: The Jakarta attack and reports of ISIS targeting Kuala Lumpur show ISIS' global strategy includes hitting Southeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The recent attack in Jakarta and news reports of ISIS targeting locations in Kuala Lumpur have shown us that ISIS' global strategy includes hitting us, in our very own backyard here in Southeast Asia.

sections.label: Military role in major terror attack
sections.summary: The Home Team has foiled terrorist threats, but a large-scale armed attack may require the military to engage perpetrators and restore public confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Thus far, the Home Team has done an excellent job in keeping Singapore safe and has anticipated and foiled a number of potential terrorist threats by identifying and arresting key people in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: However, in the event of a major terror attack, say along the lines of Mumbai or Paris, which we hope will never happen in Singapore, but where the attack is large scale and the perpetrators are armed with firearms and bombs and hundreds are killed or injured, it may be necessary for the military to step in both to engage and eliminate the perpetrators as well as to restore public confidence.

sections.label: Bangladeshi Central bank hacking
sections.summary: Hackers stole about $101 million from Bangladeshi Central bank accounts at the US Federal Reserve, with funds channelled abroad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: On cybercrime, recently, there was a shocking report that hackers had hacked into the Bangladeshi Central bank accounts in New York with the Federal Reserve and stolen some $101 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: An investigation by US cyber forensic expert Fire Eye revealed that much of this money had been channelled to accounts abroad, including places like the Philippines and Sri Lanka.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: We understand that the hackers had originally tried to wire out more than $1 billion but the US Federal Reserve managed to block some $850 million of this from being transferred out.

sections.label: Singpass hacking incident 2014
sections.summary: In 2014 a man cracked about 300 Singpass user accounts and sold personal data to a China-based gang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: An example is the Singpass hacking incident back in 2014 where a man cracked some 300 user accounts and sold personal data to a gang based in China.

sections.label: SAF cyber defence readiness assurance
sections.summary: The question asks whether MINDEF can assure the public on SAF readiness for cyber defence and explain the threats addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, I would like to ask if MINDEF can assure the public on the readiness of SAF to handle cyber defence by explaining the types of threats it seeks to address.

sections.label: Further MINDEF cyber capabilities
sections.summary: The question asks what further capabilities MINDEF intends to develop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, what further capabilities does MINDEF intend to develop?

sections.label: Defence relations with US and China
sections.summary: The question asks for an update on Singapore's defence relations with the US and China over the past year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In this regard, two of the major powers that operate in this region are the US and China and both play an important role in the security and stability of the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I was quite happy to know that Singapore has entered into a Defence Cooperation Agreement with the US as well as a Four-Point Consensus with China that will help deepen ties between these two countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide an update on its defence relations with the US and China in the past year?

sections.label: Singapore-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
sections.summary: In June 2015 Lee Hsien Loong and Tony Abbott signed the CSP, aiming to deepen cooperation in four fields through Project 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: In June 2015, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong and then-Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott signed the Singapore-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under CSP, the two countries aim to deepen cooperation across four fields: trade and economics, foreign affairs, defence and security, and people-to-people ties through a roadmap known as Project 2025.

sections.label: CSP defence implications and ADMM-Plus
sections.summary: Lee announced a defence cooperation agreement for 2016, and ADMM-Plus was convened as a platform between ASEAN and eight dialogue partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: At the signing of CSP, Prime Minister Lee announced that Singapore and Australia also intend to conclude a defence cooperation agreement in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, what are the defence implications of CSP and how is MINDEF working to enhance defence relations with Australia?

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: It was set up as the highest defence consultative and cooperative mechanism in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Four years later, ADMM-Plus was convened to serve as a platform for practical cooperation between ASEAN member states and eight dialogue partners, namely, Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, Republic of Korea, Russian Federation and the US.

sections.label: Defence white papers
sections.summary: China issued its first white paper in 1998 and Japan in 2005, and Australia briefed China and Indonesia before its 2016 white paper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: China issued its first one in 1998 and Japan in 2005.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When informing members of the public about the immediate security environment, the strategic direction of the military and its core mission, such white papers are effective in answering why there is a need to have a strong and determined force that is able to defend the sovereignty of the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, before the latest 2016 Australian defence white paper was launched, Australia briefed China and Indonesia – two key partners – about its intention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More than a decade ago, the ASEAN Regional Forum suggested that defence white papers be published and exchanged.

sections.label: MINDEF section in expenditure document
sections.summary: The section on MINDEF comprises only eight pages of the Government's expenditure control document for FY 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, it is noteworthy that the section on MINDEF comprises only eight pages of the Government's expenditure control document for financial year (FY) 2016.

sections.label: Local defence science and technology capabilities
sections.summary: The SAF procures equipment overseas but has also built local defence science and technology capabilities through investments in personnel, facilities, technology and R&D.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While the SAF does procure equipment and platforms from overseas, it has also been building Singapore's local defence science and technology capabilities through investments in personnel, facilities, technology and research and development (R&D) in complex defence systems.

sections.label: SAF counter-terrorism preparedness questions
sections.summary: The member asks how well the SAF is prepared for counter-terrorism and whether it would augment the Home Team in such operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Although the SAF has participated in many MOOTW operations, I believe the training syllabus of full-time National Servicemen (NSFs) and NSmen is still largely based on conventional armed conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: How well is the SAF prepared as regards intelligence, technology and equipment to deal with counter-terrorism?

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Also, would the SAF be called upon to augment the Home Team in counter-terrorism operations over and above the protection of key installations, which I understand the SAF does today?

sections.label: SAF personnel for major disasters
sections.summary: The Member asks the Minister whether the SAF has sufficiently trained personnel to deploy in major disasters in the region or worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Given that disasters will occur every now and then, whether here or abroad, I would like to ask the Minister if the SAF has sufficiently trained personnel to deploy in the event of major disasters in the region or around the world.

sections.label: Low population and National Service recruits
sections.summary: The Member asks how the SAF can maintain capabilities and capacity given a critically low replacement rate and fewer recruits per cohort.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: Our population replacement rate for Singapore is critically low and, with this, fewer babies are born each year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: This also will translate to fewer recruits per cohort for National Service.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: How can SAF maintain our capabilities and capacity in view of these "shrinking" manpower numbers?

sections.label: Technology investment and decreasing manpower
sections.summary: The Member asks whether investment in technology and IT can help cope with and compensate for decreasing manpower numbers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: Is this investment in technology and IT able to help us cope and compensate for our decreasing manpower numbers?

sections.label: Terrorism as clear threat
sections.summary: The passage states that the clear and present threat upon Singapore is terrorism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The clear and present threat upon us is terrorism.

sections.label: ISIS threat compared to Al-Qaeda
sections.summary: The passage states ISIS threat levels for Singapore are higher than Al-Qaeda and Jemaah Islamiyah, and ISIS exceeded Al-Qaeda's numbers in three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Threat levels for Singapore from ISIS are higher than those posed by Al-Qaeda (AQ) and Jemaah Islamiyah (JI) when they were active.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: So, if you would like a simple number, what Al-Qaeda was able to attract − both sympathisers and operatives − in the last 10 years, ISIS has already exceeded the number in the last three years.

sections.label: Malaysian Police on ISIS funding
sections.summary: The passage states Malaysian Police revealed this week that ISIS allocated around S$100,000 to Katibah Nusantara.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Just this week, the Malaysian Police revealed that ISIS had allocated around S$100,000 to Katibah Nusantara − a network that Mr Vikram Nair pointed out.

sections.label: Southeast Asians joining Iraq Syria fight
sections.summary: Close to a thousand people from Southeast Asia, including Singaporeans, travelled to Iraq and Syria in the past year to join the fight.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In the past year, close to a thousand people from Southeast Asia have travelled to Iraq and Syria to join the fight, including Singaporeans.

sections.label: ISIS newsletter names Singapore enemy
sections.summary: Last year the ISIS-published English-language newsletter Dabiq named Singapore among the enemies of the Islamic State and called for jihad against it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Last year, Dabiq − "Dabiq" is an English-language newsletter published by ISIS − named Singapore among the "enemies of the Islamic State" and called on followers to wage jihad against us.

sections.label: Changi Airport passenger numbers
sections.summary: Changi Airport received over 55 million passengers last year, and many more crossed Singapore's land and sea checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Changi Airport received over 55 million passengers last year, and many more crossed land and sea checkpoints of Singapore.

sections.label: Indonesia destroys foreign fishing boats
sections.summary: Since President Joko Widodo took office in 2014, Indonesia has confiscated and destroyed approximately 150 foreign fishing boats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Since President Joko Widodo took office in 2014, Indonesia has confiscated and destroyed approximately 150 foreign fishing boats.

sections.label: Asia defence spending exceeds Europe
sections.summary: Since 2012 Asia has collectively spent more on defence than Europe in absolute dollars, with rising nationalism and improving economies driving military modernisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In fact, collectively, Asia has spent more on its defence than Europe, in absolute dollars, since 2012.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Rising nationalism and improving economies have fuelled many Asian countries to spend larger and larger sums to modernise their militaries.

sections.label: Ageing population and social spending
sections.summary: In 2030 Singapore will have nearly one million people above 65, its workforce is declining and social spending needs to go up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Even in the 1960s and 1970s, when our needs were going up, we reaped our demographic dividend.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: But in 2030, we will have nearly one million people above 65 years old, our workforce is declining and our social spending needs to go up.

sections.label: Defence expenditure growth trajectory
sections.summary: Defence expenditure has grown about 4% annually in nominal terms over the past decade, and the same trajectory is expected to be maintained.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Our defence expenditure has roughly kept pace with inflation, growing by about 4% annually in nominal terms over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: I expect to maintain the same trajectory in the longer term, but we have to watch inflation and see if there is deflation or lower rise of inflation.

sections.label: ISIS hybrid warfare tactics
sections.summary: ISIS employs hybrid warfare skilfully and exploits social media in sophisticated ways to target the young and innocent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For example, ISIS employs hybrid warfare skilfully and exploits social media in sophisticated ways to target the young and innocent.

sections.label: Singapore susceptibility to hybrid threats
sections.summary: Singapore is particularly susceptible to hybrid threats because it is an open economy connected to the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Singapore is particularly susceptible to hybrid threats because we are an open economy and connected to the world.

sections.label: SAF adapting to wider threats
sections.summary: The previous SAF construct centred on combined arms was inadequate for non-traditional security challenges, and the SAF must adapt as threats widen and evolve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: It was, as Mr Cedric Foo pointed out, that the previous SAF construct could not have addressed this wider spectrum of threats decisively because the previous structures of the SAF, as Members here know, centred on combined arms within the Army, with a competent Air Force and Navy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: They would have been inadequate to deal with non-traditional security challenges – natural disasters or hybrid threats, such as cyberattacks or terrorism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: But as Members have pointed out, the spectrum of today's threats continues to widen and evolve and the SAF must adapt.

sections.label: Special Operations Task Force composition
sections.summary: The Special Operations Task Force is drawn from the Commandos, Naval Diving Unit and assets across the three Services, and will be the SAF's first responders.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The Special Operations Task Force (SOTF) is drawn from the Commandos, the Naval Diving Unit and assets from across the three Services and they will be our SAF's first responders in counter-terrorism and other contingency operations.

sections.label: SOTF response and neutralisation capability
sections.summary: The SOTF must be able to respond faster when activated and neutralise armed attackers in addition to hostage rescue.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The SOTF must have the capability to respond even faster when activated, and have the means to neutralise armed attackers, in addition to hostage rescue.

sections.label: Peacekeeper Protected Response Vehicle
sections.summary: The Peacekeeper Protected Response Vehicle was commissioned last year to give responders greater mobility, protection and more precise firepower.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: These units will be better equipped to perform their tasks.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: So, for example, we commissioned last year the Peacekeeper Protected Response Vehicle (PRV), which will give our responders greater mobility, protection and more precise firepower to deal decisively with threats.

sections.label: New urban training facility
sections.summary: SAF has decided to build a new high-density urban training facility with high-rise buildings, mock-up transport nodes and complex road networks.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: SAF has decided to build a new high-density urban training facility and this will have features, such as high-rise buildings, mock-up transport nodes and complex road networks.

sections.label: IAT deployment extended
sections.summary: Commanders commended the efforts and asked SAF to continue the IAT deployment, which was extended for another year this year.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The commanders there have commended our efforts and asked the SAF to continue the IAT deployment which we have extended for another year this year.

sections.label: SAF command of Combined Task Force 151
sections.summary: The SAF most recently took over command of the Combined Task Force 151 for the fourth time for counter-piracy efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Most recently, the SAF took over command of the Combined Task Force 151 for the fourth time for our counter-piracy efforts.

sections.label: New SAF Engineering Scholarship
sections.summary: A new SAF Engineering Scholarship will be introduced to attract bright young individuals to join SAF as military engineers.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Ms Jessica Tan asked how we can continue to compete for defence engineering scholars.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: We will introduce a new SAF Engineering Scholarship to attract bright young individuals with the interest and commitment to join SAF as military engineers.

sections.label: Littoral Mission Vessels acquisition
sections.summary: The Navy is acquiring eight Littoral Mission Vessels to replace Patrol Vessels, with the first launched in July last year.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The Navy is acquiring eight versatile Littoral Mission Vessels (LMVs) to replace our long-serving Patrol Vessels.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The first LMV, Independence, was launched in July last year and is expected to be operational by early next year.

sections.label: Cyber Defence Operations Hub headcount
sections.summary: Questions on national security should go to that agency, and the SAF's Cyber Defence Operations Hub headcount will double by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Some of the Members' specific questions on national security should be put to that agency.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: But for the SAF, as Mr Low rightly pointed out, what we set up recently was a Cyber Defence Operations Hub (CDOH).

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: I will not give Members the exact numbers but I will just say that we will double the headcount by 2020.

sections.label: Enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement
sections.summary: Last December the enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement was concluded, updating and deepening defence ties to cover counter-terrorism, biosecurity and cyber defence.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Last December, US Secretary of Defense Ashton Carter and I concluded the enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: This agreement updates and deepens our defence ties to cover non-conventional security areas, such as counter-terrorism, biosecurity and cyber defence.

sections.label: ADMM-Plus exercise and Total Defence
sections.summary: Singapore will co-organise this year's ADMM-Plus Maritime Security and Counter-Terrorism Exercise involving 18 militaries, while the ISIS threat makes Total Defence more relevant.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: For example, the ADMM-Plus Maritime Security and Counter-Terrorism Exercise will be conducted this year, which Singapore will co-organise.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: It will involve 18 militaries and build trust among one another and reduce the risk of mishaps at sea.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: But the threat that we now face from extremist groups like ISIS makes Total Defence more relevant than ever.

sections.label: Poll on defence performance
sections.summary: In last August's polls, 97% of Singaporean respondents felt the Government had performed well in defence and national security.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: In last August's polls, 97% of Singaporean respondents felt that the Government had performed well in defence and national security.

sections.label: Apache helicopter engines failure
sections.summary: Six years ago both engines of an Apache helicopter failed mid-flight, and the airmen glided in free fall from 10,000 feet to avoid risking civilian lives.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Six years ago, both engines of one of our Apache helicopters failed mid-flight.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: But they acted professionally and, as every airman is taught, ensured that civilian lives were not put at risk, even if it meant endangering their own.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: They glided in free fall from 10,000 feet, reached the ground in two minutes.

sections.label: LTA Kamalasivam saves recruit
sections.summary: Three years ago, LTA Kamalasivam put his life on the line to save a recruit during a live grenade exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Three years ago, LTA Kamalasivam, put his life on the line to save a recruit during a live grenade exercise.

sections.label: SAF lives of Singaporeans first
sections.summary: The speaker says that for the SAF, the lives of Singaporeans must come first, naming MAJ Quek, MAJ Ler and LTA Kamalasivam receiving the SAF Medal for Distinguished Act.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Ultimately, I would say, for the SAF, the lives of Singaporeans must come first.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: That is MAJ Quek and MAJ Ler, and that is LTA Kamalasivam receiving the SAF Medal for Distinguished Act on SAF Day.

sections.label: Deploying NSmen to NS units
sections.summary: One suggestion is to consider how more NSmen can be deployed to NS units more quickly, ideally not more than two years after their operationally-ready date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: One suggestion is to consider how more NSmen can be deployed to the NS units more quickly than before; ideally not more than two years after their operationally-ready date.

sections.label: Make-up ICTs and SkillsFuture credits
sections.summary: The speaker asks about make-up high-key ICTs in SAF NS units and asks MINDEF to consider topping up NSmen's SkillsFuture credits during their NS training cycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: To what extent have SAF NS units been able to implement make-up high-key ICTs as recommended by the Committee to Strengthen National Service (CSNS)?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: However, in view of the renewed impetus towards lifelong learning and particularly SkillsFuture, can I ask MINDEF, when it next reviews its NS policies, to consider topping up the accounts of NSmen with additional SkillsFuture credits through the course of their NS training cycle in recognition of their lifelong commitment towards National Service?

sections.label: CSNS recommendations and NS HOME Awards
sections.summary: CSNS made recommendations in five areas, and MINDEF announced the revamp of the NSRA into the NS HOME Awards, providing additional MediSave and MediShield Life grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Based on feedback, CSNS made recommendations in five areas: (a) strengthening NS training system; (b) increasing opportunities for NSmen to contribute; (c) establishing the SAF Volunteer Corps (SAFVC); (d) enhancing recognition and benefits for NSmen; and (e) expanding community support for NSmen.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, MINDEF also announced the revamp of the National Service Recognition Award (NSRA) into the NS HOME (Housing, Medical and Education) Awards, which will provide additional MediSave and MediShield Life grants.

sections.label: Free MediShield Life coverage for NSmen
sections.summary: The speaker suggests considering other quantifiable ways of taking care of NSmen, such as free MediShield Life coverage when they are 60 years old and above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since our NSmen contributed and played an important role in our country's security, perhaps we should consider other quantifiable way of taking care of them, such as providing them free coverage through MediShield Life when they are 60 years old and above.

sections.label: Psychological issues in disability definition
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MINDEF will consider including psychological issues such as PTSD or depression arising from training or operations in its definition of disability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, will MINDEF consider including psychological issues, such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) or depression arising from training or operations, in its definition of disability?

sections.label: NS insurance and WICA compensation
sections.summary: Questions ask whether MINDEF will cover insurance costs for NS and how it assesses WICA-based compensation adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will MINDEF consider covering the full cost of insurance or co-paying private insurance when citizens serve their NS obligations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, how does MINDEF assess the adequacy of the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA)-based compensation model?

sections.label: Budget for disability and death compensation
sections.summary: Question asks the total amount MINDEF sets aside this year for long-term disability or death compensation and support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lastly, what is the total amount MINDEF sets aside for compensation and support for long-term disability or death in this year's Budget?

sections.label: Defence readiness and emergency preparedness
sections.summary: Questions ask about total defence readiness of Singaporeans and strengthening resilience, noting many lack basic emergency preparedness knowledge and skills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In view of the rising security threats, I wish to ask the Ministry the following questions: (a) what is the total defence readiness of Singaporeans; and (b) what more can be done to strengthen resilience among Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Many do not have basic emergency preparedness (EP) knowledge or skills, such as first-aid, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), automated external defibrillator (AED), and are not aware of EP response protocol.

sections.label: Halal-certified kitchens on navy vessels
sections.summary: Question asks how many active navy vessels have halal-certified kitchens, following a call to equip all vessels with them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: As such, in the COS debate last year, I urged the Minister to seriously consider the possibility of ensuring that all navy vessels are equipped with halal-certified kitchens so that Malay/Muslim Singaporeans will be able to serve freely in the navy vessels without any constraint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: If efforts have been made, how many vessels out of the total number currently in active service have halal-certified kitchens?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: I understand that SAF's deployment of our NS soldiers is based on aptitude, abilities and commitment to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The Advisory Council on Community Relations in Defence (ACCORD) serves as a channel for the community to provide feedback on issues concerning Singapore's defence.

sections.label: Resident seeks mobilisation exemption
sections.summary: A resident appealed for a 15-day exemption from a one-month mobilisation manning period because his company sent him on a five-day Europe incentive trip.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Recently, a resident came to my Meet-the-People session to appeal for a 15-day exemption from a one-month-long mobilisation manning period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: This is because his company just sent him on a five-day incentive trip to Europe for his outstanding work performance.

sections.label: Commanding Officer's reply tone
sections.summary: The passage describes a cordial professional email and surprise at the Commanding Officer's reply tone, quoting an extract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: It was a very cordial and professional email.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: So, I was quite surprised with the tone of the reply by the Commanding Officer (CO), and I quote an extract: "I still have the prerogative to fully reject his request to even go for the business trip, let alone the personal trip.

sections.label: Resident's incentive trip extension
sections.summary: A resident got permission for an incentive trip but not its extension, and the CO could have been friendlier to the appealing company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: It is not as simple as you may think." I am glad that my resident eventually managed to get permission to go on his incentive trip, but not the extension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: However, I feel that the CO could have been friendlier and understanding when he dealt with the company which was appealing for its staff.

sections.label: Motorised Infantry Simulator Centre
sections.summary: The Motorised Infantry Simulator Centre was launched in October 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: One example is the Motorised Infantry Simulator Centre, launched in October 2015.

sections.label: Compensation framework and medical expenses
sections.summary: The compensation framework is more generous than WICA, paying two to four times WICA amounts, and MINDEF pays medical expenses for service-related injuries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our compensation framework takes reference from and is more generous than that under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Any compensation amounts are generally two to four times that provided under WICA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MINDEF also pays for all necessary medical expenses incurred at Government and restructured hospitals or clinics for the treatment of service-related injury, for as long as required.

sections.label: ORNS cycle reduction
sections.summary: Since 2006, the ORNS cycle was reduced from 13 years to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Since 2006, we were able to reduce the ORNS cycle from 13 years to 10 years.

sections.label: Awards and celebratory gifts
sections.summary: Coverage rises from top 10% to top 30%, with $200 and $100 awards, plus $100 vouchers for marriage or a new child.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, it is the top 10%; it will increase to the top 30%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The top 10% will receive $200 while the next 20% will receive $100, which is the amount awarded today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will also be introducing Celebratory Gifts for NSmen.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They will receive $100 worth of vouchers when they get married or welcome a new child into their families.

sections.label: Servicemen insurance coverage
sections.summary: Each serviceman is covered for $150,000 in group term life and group personal accident insurance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Each serviceman will be covered for $150,000 in group term life and in group personal accident insurance.

sections.label: NS Mark accreditation scheme
sections.summary: A national accreditation scheme, the NS Mark, will be launched this year, awarding organisations NS Mark, NS Mark (Gold), or NS Advocate status.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To better recognise such companies, this year, we will launch a national accreditation scheme, the NS Mark.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Under the scheme, organisations will be awarded either the NS Mark or the higher-tiered NS Mark (Gold), and top NS Mark (Gold) organisations will be further recognised as NS Advocates.

sections.label: NSmen join Expertise Conversion Scheme
sections.summary: NSmen with expertise in engineering and psychology have volunteered for the Expertise Conversion Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For instance, NSmen with the relevant expertise in engineering and psychology have volunteered for the Expertise Conversion Scheme.

sections.label: SAF Volunteer Corps volunteers
sections.summary: Women, new citizens and first-generation PRs serve in the SAF Volunteer Corps; last year 226 volunteers completed Basic Training and over 80% progressed further.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This spirit is also demonstrated by women, new citizens and first-generation Permanent Residents (PRs) who have come forth to serve in the SAF Volunteer Corps (SAFVC), which Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef had asked about.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are proud that last year, 226 volunteers from a diverse range of backgrounds and ages completed their Basic Training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: More than 80% of the Volunteers have progressed to the next phases of training.

sections.label: First 2016 Basic Training intake
sections.summary: The first intake for 2016 completed their Basic Training last week.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Just last week, the first intake for 2016 completed their Basic Training.

sections.label: Self-radicalised youth detained
sections.summary: A self-radicalised youth was detained in April last year after a friend alerted authorities before he could carry out attack plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, a self-radicalised youth was detained in April last year after a friend noticed changes in him and alerted the authorities before he could carry out his attack plans in Singapore.

sections.label: SAF operational priorities before individual needs
sections.summary: The SAF will accommodate where it can, but its operational priorities come before individual needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: SAF will accommodate where we can, but the SAF's operational priorities come before individual needs.

sections.label: MINDEF ACCORD NS support update
sections.summary: ACCORD implemented 14 of 18 proposals to strengthen NS support, including business discounts, women's outreach and a polytechnic fitness programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Mr Baey Yam Keng asked for an update on the work MINDEF has done to strengthen the community's support for NS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: I am pleased to update that ACCORD has implemented 14 out of 18 proposals submitted last year to strengthen support for NS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: First, the Family and Community (F&C) Council has encouraged almost 70 businesses to show appreciation to NSmen by offering discounts and benefits through the "We Support YOU in NS" programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The F&C Council also improved their outreach to women through partnerships with the Singapore Council of Women's Organisations and the Women's Integration Network of the People's Association.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: At Temasek Polytechnic, for example, the fitness programme increased the IPPT pass rate of participating students by more than 25%.

sections.label: NS Advocate Award recipients
sections.summary: Last year, 122 individuals, businesses and organisations received the NS Advocate Award for outstanding support towards NS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Last year, 122 individuals, businesses and organisations were awarded the NS Advocate Award for their outstanding support towards NS.

sections.label: Army and Navy events
sections.summary: In June, the Singapore Army and RSN will hold an exhibition and Navy@Vivo, projected to reach over 250,000 visitors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Later in June, the Singapore Army and the Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN) will hold an exhibition and Navy@Vivo respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We project to reach out to over 250,000 visitors through these events.

sections.label: Song re-introduced to schools
sections.summary: The song was re-introduced to schools and reached more than 600,000 TV viewers over a 10-day period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The song was re-introduced to schools and reached more than 600,000 TV viewers over a 10-day period.

sections.label: Total Defence stories and N.E.mation
sections.summary: A Victoria Junior College student volunteered after N.E.mation!, and SAF programmes and stories aim to encourage Total Defence conversations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Hoon Wei Ting, from Victoria Junior College, was so inspired by her participation in N.E.mation! last year that she volunteered to help out and share her experience with participants this year as well.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We hope that when these competition clips are shown nationwide, they will encourage conversations about Total Defence and inspire all to do their part to keep Singapore strong and resilient.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Our stories highlight the sacrifices our NSmen make and the tough training they undergo to defend Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Programmes, such as the "Commandos" documentary series, "Women in the SAF" and "SAF Pioneers" were all well-received.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are heartened that Singaporeans' commitment to defence remains strong, and we will continue to share more of our stories in the coming year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: After 50 years of nationhood, the threats we are facing have evolved, but so have our responses.

sections.label: NS Mark Scheme details timing
sections.summary: Details of the NS Mark Scheme will be announced in the latter part of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for the details of the NS Mark Scheme, they will be announced in the latter part of the year.

sections.label: National coordinating agency CSA
sections.summary: The CSA is Singapore's national coordinating agency for whole-of-Government matters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The national coordinating agency for Singapore and whole-of-Government is the CSA.

sections.label: Redeploying make-up high-key ICT
sections.summary: Make-up high-key ICT personnel are redeployed to another unit undergoing a high-key ICT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Of course, make-up high-key ICT is to redeploy them to another unit which is going through a high-key ICT.

sections.label: Muslim cookhouses and vegetarian food
sections.summary: Where practicable, camps with adequate space have Muslim cookhouses and vegetarian food served.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I think Senior Minister of State Maliki was very clear: where it is practicable, we will lean forward; the SAF, as with the rest of society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, in camps where there is adequate space, as Members know, we have Muslim cookhouses, vegetarian food is served.

sections.label: Volunteer training three phases
sections.summary: The training differs from full-time NS training, has three phases, and is structured by volunteers' physical abilities and interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The training is different from the full-time NS training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is in three different phases and it will be structured according to the physical abilities and also the interests of the volunteers.

sections.label: Withdrawing amendment and NS discussion
sections.summary: The Speaker asks Mr Vikram Nair to withdraw his amendment after a lively discussion about NS in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Mr Vikram Nair, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I think we have had a very lively discussion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In Singapore, because we have NS, I think almost everyone is either serving in the military or know someone who is serving in the military.
